subject: chemistry

concepts.title: Standard Cell Potential
concepts.definition: The potential difference between cathode and anode electrodes under standard thermodynamic conditions with zero net current flow.
concepts.key_idea: Standard cell EMF is calculated by subtracting the anode standard reduction potential from the cathode standard reduction potential.
question_patterns: calculate standard cell potential from electrode potentials
find the standard emf of a galvanic cell
determine the cell potential under standard conditions
evaluate standard electromotive force given cathode and anode reduction potentials
what is the standard cell voltage for the redox pair

solution_steps.action: Subtract anode potential from cathode potential
solution_steps.explain: Standard EMF is given by right-hand electrode potential minus left-hand electrode potential.

solution_steps.action: Identify cathode and anode from reduction potentials
solution_steps.explain: The electrode with higher standard reduction potential acts as cathode (reduction), the lower one as anode (oxidation).

solution_steps.action: Verify spontaneity of the cell reaction
solution_steps.explain: A positive E_cell value confirms the redox reaction is thermodynamically spontaneous under standard conditions.

concepts.title: Nernst Equation for Cell EMF
concepts.definition: An equation expressing electrode or cell electromotive force as a function of standard cell potential and reaction quotient.
concepts.key_idea: Non-standard cell potential depends logarithmically on the ratio of product ion concentrations to reactant ion concentrations.
question_patterns: calculate non-standard cell potential using Nernst equation
find the cell emf at specified ion concentrations
determine electromotive force for non-unit concentration cell
evaluate cell potential when reactant and product concentrations vary
what is the cell voltage given standard potential and log reaction quotient

solution_steps.action: Calculate voltage drop due to reaction quotient
solution_steps.explain: Multiply 0.059 by reaction quotient log divided by transferred electron count.

solution_steps.action: Subtract voltage drop from standard cell potential
solution_steps.explain: Cell EMF under non-standard conditions is standard EMF minus concentration drop term.

solution_steps.action: Verify cell spontaneity under non-standard conditions
solution_steps.explain: If E_cell is positive the cell reaction is spontaneous at the given concentrations; a negative value indicates non-spontaneity.

concepts.title: Equilibrium Constant from Nernst Equation
concepts.definition: The exact relationship connecting standard electrode potential of a cell with the equilibrium constant of its overall cell reaction at 298 K.
concepts.key_idea: At chemical equilibrium the cell potential becomes zero, directly linking standard cell potential to the equilibrium constant.
question_patterns: calculate equilibrium constant log value from standard cell potential
find log Kc for a cell reaction given standard emf
determine equilibrium constant exponent from standard electrode potentials
evaluate logarithm of Kc using electron number and standard potential
what is the value of log Kc for the redox reaction

solution_steps.action: Multiply transferred electron number by standard potential
solution_steps.explain: Calculate total standard voltage scaled by electron charge factor.

solution_steps.action: Divide product by Nernst constant 0.059
solution_steps.explain: Logarithm of equilibrium constant is proportional to standard potential times electron count.

solution_steps.action: Compute the equilibrium constant from its logarithm
solution_steps.explain: Take the antilogarithm to obtain the actual equilibrium constant Kc from log Kc.

concepts.title: Standard Gibbs Energy of Cell Reaction
concepts.definition: The standard free energy change of an electrochemical reaction derived from standard cell potential and electron stoichiometry.
concepts.key_idea: Electrical work obtainable from a cell equals the negative change in standard Gibbs free energy.
question_patterns: calculate standard Gibbs energy change for cell reaction
find standard free energy from cell emf and charge
determine delta G standard given standard potential and Faraday constant
evaluate maximum work done by galvanic cell reaction
what is the standard Gibbs free energy change in joules per mole

solution_steps.action: Calculate standard Gibbs free energy change
solution_steps.explain: Multiply negative charge transferred by standard cell potential.

solution_steps.action: Calculate total charge transferred during the reaction
solution_steps.explain: Total charge equals the number of moles of electrons multiplied by Faraday constant.

solution_steps.action: Verify thermodynamic feasibility of the cell reaction
solution_steps.explain: A negative delta_G confirms the cell reaction is spontaneous; the magnitude indicates maximum useful electrical work obtainable.

concepts.title: Resistivity and Conductivity of Electrolytes
concepts.definition: The intrinsic material property quantifying resistance to charge transport across a defined cross-sectional electrolyte column.
concepts.key_idea: Resistivity is directly proportional to solution resistance and area of cross-section, inversely proportional to column length.
question_patterns: calculate resistivity of electrolyte solution column
find specific resistance from resistance and dimensions
determine electrical resistivity given area length and resistance
evaluate electrolyte resistivity from column geometry
what is the solution resistivity in ohm cm

solution_steps.action: Multiply resistance by cross-sectional area
solution_steps.explain: Form product of resistance and cross section.

solution_steps.action: Divide by column length
solution_steps.explain: Resistivity equals resistance times area divided by length.

solution_steps.action: Compute conductivity from resistivity
solution_steps.explain: Conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity and characterizes the ease of ion transport through the electrolyte.

concepts.title: Cell Constant and Solution Conductivity
concepts.definition: The geometric ratio of distance between electrodes to their effective area, evaluated by measuring resistance of a standard solution.
concepts.key_idea: Cell constant depends purely on cell geometry and equals resistance times standard conductivity.
question_patterns: calculate cell constant from solution resistance and conductivity
find cell constant G star for conductivity cell
determine cell factor using standard KCl solution data
evaluate conductivity cell constant in inverse centimeters
what is the cell constant given resistance and conductivity

solution_steps.action: Multiply measured resistance by known specific conductivity
solution_steps.explain: Cell constant G star equals resistance times conductivity.

solution_steps.action: Determine unknown solution conductivity using the cell constant
solution_steps.explain: Once the cell constant is known, conductivity of any solution is found by dividing cell constant by its measured resistance.

solution_steps.action: Verify dimensional consistency of the cell constant
solution_steps.explain: Cell constant has units of inverse length (cm-1 or m-1), confirming it depends only on electrode geometry and not on the solution.

concepts.title: Molar Conductivity of Electrolytic Solutions
concepts.definition: The total electrical conducting capability of all ions formed by one mole of dissolved electrolyte at given concentration.
concepts.key_idea: Molar conductivity scales solution conductivity by total volume containing one mole of dissolved electrolyte.
question_patterns: calculate molar conductivity from specific conductivity and concentration
find molar conductivity of electrolyte solution
determine molar conductance given conductivity and molarity
evaluate lambda m in S cm2 per mol
what is the molar conductivity for given salt solution

solution_steps.action: Multiply conductivity by conversion factor 1000
solution_steps.explain: Scale conductivity to volume-equivalent molar units.

solution_steps.action: Divide scaled conductivity by concentration in molarity
solution_steps.explain: Molar conductivity is scaled conductivity divided by molarity.

solution_steps.action: Compare molar conductivity with limiting molar conductivity
solution_steps.explain: The ratio of molar conductivity at a given concentration to limiting molar conductivity indicates the degree of dissociation of the electrolyte.

concepts.title: Kohlrausch Law of Independent Migration of Ions
concepts.definition: A fundamental law stating limiting molar conductivity of an electrolyte equals sum of individual limiting molar conductivities of constituent ions.
concepts.key_idea: At infinite dilution each ion migrates independently, contributing a constant characteristic value to total molar conductivity.
question_patterns: calculate limiting molar conductivity using Kohlrausch law
find total limiting molar conductivity from ionic conductivities
determine limiting molar conductance for salt electrolyte
evaluate lambda m deg using individual ion contributions
what is the limiting molar conductivity of electrolyte at infinite dilution

solution_steps.action: Calculate cation contribution
solution_steps.explain: Multiply number of cations by individual cation limiting conductivity.

solution_steps.action: Calculate anion contribution
solution_steps.explain: Multiply number of anions by individual anion limiting conductivity.

solution_steps.action: Sum ionic contributions
solution_steps.explain: Add cation and anion contributions to obtain limiting molar conductivity.

concepts.title: Degree of Dissociation of Weak Electrolytes
concepts.definition: The fraction of weak electrolyte solute molecules dissociated into ions at a specific solution concentration.
concepts.key_idea: Degree of dissociation equals ratio of molar conductivity at concentration c to limiting molar conductivity at infinite dilution.
question_patterns: calculate degree of dissociation alpha for weak electrolyte
find fraction of dissociated weak acid molecules
determine degree of ionization from molar conductivities
evaluate alpha given lambda m and limiting lambda m deg
what is the degree of dissociation for weak acid solution

solution_steps.action: Divide molar conductivity by limiting molar conductivity
solution_steps.explain: Degree of dissociation alpha is ratio of molar conductivity to limiting molar conductivity.

solution_steps.action: Calculate the dissociation constant of the weak electrolyte
solution_steps.explain: Using Ostwald dilution law, the dissociation constant Ka relates alpha and concentration C as Ka = C * alpha^2 / (1 - alpha).

solution_steps.action: Verify the weak electrolyte behavior
solution_steps.explain: For a weak electrolyte alpha is much less than 1, confirming partial dissociation and validating the Ostwald approximation.

concepts.title: Electric Charge in Electrolysis
concepts.definition: The total quantitative electric charge passed through an electrolytic cell during an electrolysis process.
concepts.key_idea: Total electric charge in coulombs equals electric current in amperes multiplied by time in seconds.
question_patterns: calculate charge passed during electrolysis
find quantity of electricity in coulombs
determine total charge given current and time duration
evaluate charge transferred across electrolytic wire
what is the quantity of charge in coulombs for given current and time

solution_steps.action: Multiply electric current by time in seconds
solution_steps.explain: Charge Q equals steady current I times duration t.

solution_steps.action: Convert charge to moles of electrons
solution_steps.explain: Divide total charge by Faraday constant to obtain the number of moles of electrons transferred during electrolysis.

solution_steps.action: Relate moles of electrons to moles of substance deposited
solution_steps.explain: Divide moles of electrons by the stoichiometric number of electrons per mole of product to find moles of substance transformed.

concepts.title: Mass Deposited in Electrolysis
concepts.definition: Faraday's first law quantitative relationship governing mass of substance deposited or liberated at an electrode during electrolysis.
concepts.key_idea: Deposited mass is directly proportional to electric charge passed and element equivalent mass.
question_patterns: calculate mass of metal deposited during electrolysis
find weight of element liberated at cathode
determine mass deposited given current duration and stoichiometry
evaluate yield of electrodeposited metal using Faraday law
what is the mass of metal deposited at electrode in grams

solution_steps.action: Calculate total electric charge
solution_steps.explain: Multiply steady current by duration in seconds.

solution_steps.action: Calculate mass of deposited substance
solution_steps.explain: Mass equals molar mass times charge passed divided by electrons transferred times Faraday constant.

solution_steps.action: Verify the deposited mass against Faraday first law proportionality
solution_steps.explain: The calculated mass should be directly proportional to the total charge passed, confirming Faraday first law of electrolysis.

concepts.title: Batteries, Fuel Cells and Corrosion Mechanism
concepts.definition: Principles governing commercial primary cells, secondary rechargeable batteries, continuous fuel cells, and electrochemical metallic corrosion.
concepts.key_idea: Batteries convert chemical energy directly into electrical work through spontaneous localized half-cell redox reactions.
question_patterns: describe chemical working of primary or secondary batteries
explain electrode half-reactions in fuel cell
how does lead storage battery operate during discharge and charge
explain corrosion of iron as an electrochemical process
differentiate primary and secondary battery systems

solution_steps.action: Identify anodic oxidation process
solution_steps.explain: Substance undergoes electron loss at anode oxidation site.

solution_steps.action: Identify cathodic reduction process
solution_steps.explain: Oxidizing species accepts electrons at cathodic site.

solution_steps.action: Combine half-reactions for net cell process
solution_steps.explain: Sum half-cell reactions to verify overall cell chemical transformation.
